NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
Why these decisions, measured against the current write path, not inherited from the charter sentence.
Command home. F86.2 listed the live roots and noted that gate already has four subcommands while spec and plan expose new only. Adding a root moves liveCommandRoots and the README CLI Overview tables; that is what those pins are for. Putting the verb under gate would be the cheaper command-surface edit and the worse product: GateId is closed at src/gates/ledger.ts:103 to approve, apply, archive; verdict is already the special case that records without being a GateId; C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT revised A29.2 for approve only. A status-writing directory move under gate would be a second purity hole, and would teach that every lifecycle close is a gate even when nothing is evaluated. Putting it under spec (or plan) would name one artifact and then write the other plus move the directory. A top-level supersede root is the thing the operator says.
Implementation home. The sanctioned status writer is writeDraftRootToApproved / stampApproveArtifact in src/gates/ledger.ts. This verb is a sibling export in that file so the writeFileSync allowlist does not grow a path. The command def itself follows scaffoldCommand: an extra root exported from src/grace-generate.ts, already in package.json files, already allowed to writeFileSync. A new src/grace-supersede.ts would need a files-list line or the packed CLI would ship a help entry with no module (F99 class). That cost is avoided without hiding the root.
Require, do not create. The registry says atomically with the replacement. F86.2 says the replacement directory must already exist or lint is red. Those are not the same claim. Creating a skeleton would duplicate spec new, and would leave the operator authoring the successor after the old contract had been archived. ngrace-plan already says create-then-mark. The only currently-legal order is replacement-first. The verb should perform that order, not invert it. Atomically means the four artifact writes and the move, including the Replacement element, are one invocation against a successor that already has a directory.
Failure. The honest intermediate states are unrepresentable (F19.1, F86.2). Validate first. Write, then renameSync. renameSync of a directory on one filesystem is the closest thing this process has to an atomic move; the lint-red window is the gap between the last writeFileSync and that rename. On throw, restore original bytes while still under active/. That is writeAndVerifyLedger's priorBytes restore (src/gates/ledger.ts:248-249) applied to spec/plan, without the unlinkSync of a newly created file, because these files already existed. A killed process that leaves superseded in active/ is the lint error the brief names; the same verb resumes by recognizing matching superseded bytes and doing only the rename. copy-into-archive then rmSync-active would produce two directories with the same C-* id for a window, and there is no change.duplicate-bundle-id check; it would also add an rmSync call site the A15.1 pin forbids.
Shape. Three accepted forms, one corpus writer. All three superseded archives write a Replacement element as the first child of the wrapper. Tests plant the other two. The verb writes the corpus shape. Closing the checker would be a grammar change this bundle does not need and would redden any future hand-authored ReplacementChange.
Ledger. F86's sharpest finding is that the ledger ends at archive=permit and cannot show the folklore close happened. That finding is about a gate Decision standing in for a transition the gate did not perform. Supersede has no gate. Appending a Decision would require expanding GateId or lying that archive ran. The Replacement element is a lint-checked successor pointer applied-close never had. Status-on-artifact without a Decision is what F86 called a gap when a gate had already recorded permit; it is not a gap when no gate is in the story. The record of this transition is the archived bundle's status and Replacement element.

Alternatives.Alternative: gate supersede subcommand. Rejected. GateId is closed. A29.2 was revised for approve only. Archive evaluates and does not move; teaching a sibling that does both writes and a move would make the gate family a mixed evaluate-and-mutate surface. The README sentence that apply, archive, and verdict never move a bundle would have to become a lie or a special case list.

spec supersede (or plan supersede). Rejected. spec new writes one skeleton file. This verb writes spec and plan and moves the directory. ngrace-plan, not ngrace-spec, is the skill that currently describes the close.

Create the replacement skeleton inside the verb. Rejected. Duplicates writeSpecNew. Inverts replacement-first. Leaves the successor unauthored after the predecessor has left active/. The replacement is a content decision, not a filesystem side-effect of abandoning the old bundle.

Move first, then write status. Rejected. A draft or approved artifact under archive/ is change.invalid-archive-status. If the writes then fail, recovery is an archive bundle with the wrong status. Write-then-rename with byte rollback keeps the unrepresentable window inside one process.

Copy modified files into archive/C-* then rmSync active/C-*. Rejected. Two directories with one C-* id for a window, and no duplicate-id check. rmSync of the bundle directory would be a fifth call site on src/grace-cursor.test.ts:515-547.

Append a Decision with a new GateId member superseded. Rejected. Expands a closed union for an event that never evaluated requirements. Would make F86's defect (a Decision that does not mean the transition happened) into an API.
Append a Decision with gate archive. Rejected. The archive gate did not run. no-open-epoch is not a supersede requirement.

Write ReplacementChange, or a direct C-* child, or close the checker to one shape. Rejected. Corpus is Replacement. Checker plurality is already tested. Closing it is a grammar change with a blast radius this verb does not need.

New src/grace-supersede.ts plus a package.json files line. Rejected as unnecessary. scaffoldCommand already lives in src/grace-generate.ts as an extra root. A new file is honest and more expensive; the packed CLI would miss it if the files list were forgotten.

Require a lexicon phrase before the verb writes. Rejected. D19 / D20 and any supersede phrase are C-APPROVAL-SCOPE. This verb is the sanctioned writer, the same way spec new is, not a second approve gate.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Applied-close verb (lifecycle finish / P3.1) that writes applied and moves. Owner: P3.1 / C-ARCHIVE-CURSOR. This bundle is superseded-only.
D19 / D20 skill sentences and any supersede lexicon phrase. Owner: C-APPROVAL-SCOPE.
Cross-device EXDEV copy-then-delete, if a platform this CLI claims ever hits it. This bundle refuses after rollback.
A duplicate-bundle-id lint when the same C-* exists under both active/ and archive/. Not required to ship this verb; named so it is not silently dropped.

Scenarios.Scenario: Happy path, replacement first. Operator runs spec new C-NEW, authors it, then ngrace supersede with argv token change C-OLD and argv token replacement C-NEW. C-OLD spec and plan become superseded, each gain a Replacement element naming C-NEW, and the directory lands under archive/. C-NEW is untouched. Lint 0/0.
Spec-only source, matching C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE. plan.xml is absent. The verb writes spec only and moves. It does not invent a plan.

Replacement already named. Spec and plan already contain a Replacement element whose text is C-NEW, still draft or approved under active/. The verb writes status only, does not insert a second element, then moves.
Missing replacement directory. Refuse, no writes, no move, no skeleton created.
Self-replacement. Refuse. change.superseded-self-replacement is the checker this refuse satisfies in advance.
Rename throws after status writes. Original spec and plan bytes are restored under active/. Exit nonzero. Lint sees the pre-invocation tree.

Process killed after writes, before rename. Spec (and plan if present) read superseded under active/, which is change.invalid-active-status. Re-running the same command with the same replacement completes the rename and does not rewrite matching bytes.
Already archived as superseded with that replacement. Refuse, already done, nonzero. No rewrite of archive/.
Open epoch on the old bundle. The verb still moves. It does not fold and does not consult no-open-epoch. Abandoned work keeps its ledger and run/ as companions.
argv token record is not declared. An unrecognized dashed flag is refused by defineGraceCommand the same way other roots refuse one.
